messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — need decisions for Sprint Alpha on reserved pool sizing, per-tenant burst windows, and autoscale grace periods. Two pilot customers asked for predictable 2x burst for launch. Options sketched below, picking one affects pricing + SLA. Can eng/ops weigh in with risk + rough effort?
kevin (Eng): Happy to. Can you paste the two customer traffic profiles? I can run a headroom sim but need per-minute QPS and 95th pct concurrency distribution.
maria (PM): Pasted sample traces: customer A is chat-heavy 60 req/min peak with long TTK; customer B is embedding-heavy bursts ~200k tokens over 10m every 6h. (inline: see link to shared drive) We need launch criteria by Thu so legal can finish SOW.
sasha (ML): For embeddings bursts we can suggest quantized model variants to reduce GPU memory and increase pack rate. That reduces reserved capacity needs but increases slight latency variance (~30ms). Good tradeoff?
kevin (Eng): Probably yes. Two architecture proposals:

1) Fixed-reserve pools per customer sized to 1.5x baseline peak + 2x short burst band with strict preemption; easy to reason about for billing and SLOs, low infra changes, higher cost.

2) Elastic reservation + opportunistic soft-burst with prewarm tokens and a short carryover window. Lower cost but needs autoscaler work and more complex billing rules.

Estimate effort: option 1 ~ 2 dev-days + 1 SRE day for onboarding. option 2 ~ 3 sprint tasks + infra + billing changes (~3w).
alex (SRE): Ops concerns: option 1 increases tail load on shared infra; need spillover rules if several customers burst simultaneously. Option 2 requires stronger isolation tests; fallback policy must be automatic to avoid cascading latency.
jen (Sales): Customers will accept slightly higher price for predictability (option 1) for GA. Customer B would consider managed-quantized variant only if we guarantee <=5% quality delta.
maria (PM): Proposed launch criteria (draft): 1) can sustain 2x requested burst for both pilots for 10m without violating 99th latency SLOs; 2) billing/contract language reflecting burst carveouts; 3) oncall runbook for spill/fallback. OK?
kevin (Eng): I'll run a sim of worst-case concurrent bursts across regions tonight. If results look good, we can cut a minimal option-1 rollout and plan option-2 as optimization post-GA.
alex (SRE): I'll draft the runbook + incident templates. Also adding monitoring hooks: per-customer burst window, preempt events, and spillover alerts. Will post PR in #eng-oncall.
maria (PM): Awesome. Action items: kevin run sim (EOD), alex runbook (tomorrow), sasha verify quantized quality tests (2 days), jen confirm contract language with legal. Meet Fri 10am to decide final path. :calendar:
deploy-bot: Reminder — template ticket created: RDW-5832 "Sprint Alpha reserved pools launch gating". Link: https://tracker.example/RDW-5832 :robot_face:
kevin (Eng): FYI sim queued: ./bin/run_headroom --trace customerA.json --trace customerB.json --concurrent 5 --out sprints/alpha-sim.log
sasha (ML): Starting quality eval for quantized variant, running eval set now. Will report delta + confidence intervals in channel.
maria (PM): Thanks everyone. If any blockers surface, ping me.
